text:
Alex (Support): Escalation from NovusAnalytics. They report intermittent 429s and long queue times when they spike from idle to ~8-12 rps for ~20-40s. They say KV cache hit rate drops and it feels like the system is dropping queued requests rather than just slow model responses.

Alex (Support): Customer provided a quick curl repro and a sample 429. Pasting both so we can triage.

Novus (Customer): repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-NOVUS\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-base","input":"List action items...","max_tokens":100}'
```

Novus (Customer): sample 429 they observe:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-rate-limit-limit: 150
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 10
x-redwood-queue-time: 415
content-length: 128

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"burst quota exhausted","request_id":"req_2145521"}
```

DeployBot: svc=ingest runtime=runtime-2 req=req_2145521 action=reject batch_wait_ms=402 batch_size=14 kv_cache_hit=false

Priya (Oncall): Alex, please confirm Novus account type (hosted/dedicated) and full list of request_ids + time window. Also ask them to include the exact client config.

Alex (Support): They're hosted. Request ids: req_2145521, req_2145524, req_2145530. First seen 1905009870, last seen 1905009928. Customer says continuous_batching=true on their client and they use a KV prefix per-user.

Daniel (Eng Runtime): Quick notes: continuous batching will collect requests up to max_batch_size or batch_window_ms. On a sudden ramp you can end up with many concurrent small batches across nodes. If the account's burst token bucket is drained, queued batches may be rejected at dispatch -> 429s. The presence of batch_wait_ms ~400 and kv_cache_hit=false strongly suggests the requests waited in the batching queue then got rejected.

Kara (SRE): We have two controls at play here: per-account token bucket (sustained + burst) and per-node concurrency/queue limits. If a tenant consumes burst tokens quickly, the runtime will stop dispatching and reject queued requests to protect node latency. That matches these logs.

Alex (Support): Customer pasted client config:
```
client_config = {
  continuous_batching: true,
  batch_window_ms: 30,
  max_batch_size: 32,
  prefer_low_latency: false,
  kv_cache: { enabled: true, prefix_ttl: 45 }
}
```

Priya (Oncall): Tests for the customer to run before we change infra:
- Controlled ramp 0->10 rps over 30s with prefer_low_latency=true and max_batch_size=8; capture all response headers.
- Repeat with kv_cache.prefix_ttl=300 and stable keys to measure hit rate.
- Send raw request bodies so Eng Runtime can inspect key variability.

Daniel (Eng Runtime): Client-side mitigations that often help: set prefer_low_latency=true (dispatch sooner), lower batch_window_ms to 10-15 ms, reduce max_batch_size to 8-12, and add small jitter to request start times to avoid synchronized bursts. Also confirm KV keys are stable across repeated requests; tiny differences in prefixing cause cache misses.

Kara (SRE): I can apply a short-lived operational mitigation: bump Novus burst tokens + increase tenant queue depth on runtime-2 for 20 minutes while they run tests. I'll monitor cluster tail latency closely.

OpsBot: action=quota_bump account=novus-analytics delta=+45% duration=20m ticket=INC-4811

DeployBot: action=queue_increase runtime=runtime-2 tenant=novus-analytics old_depth=128 new_depth=192 ticket=INC-4811

Alex (Support): I'll pass the recommended client changes to Novus: prefer_low_latency=true, max_batch_size=8, batch_window_ms=12, increase kv prefix_ttl to 300s, and jitter. Ask them to run the two ramps and paste headers. Also let them know we've temporarily bumped burst tokens.

Novus (Customer): We'll try the changes in ~10 minutes and send headers + request bodies. Thanks.

Priya (Oncall): For our internal follow-up we need: timeline of token depletion and replenishment, per-node queue metrics, KV shard hit/miss for the window, and any runtime GC/compaction that might coincide. Daniel, please search for the request_ids and collect node-level traces.

Daniel (Eng Runtime): Will do. Quick internal todo: add an x-redwood-burst-remaining header and make x-redwood-queue-time reliable so customers can see queue wait without us digging logs. I'll file a small ticket for this.

Kara (SRE): Creating an alert rule: accounts emitting 429s with x-redwood-queue-time>300ms will generate a support ticket and page oncall during business hours. Also monitoring shows the temporary bump reduced rejects so far.

Alex (Support): I'll update Novus once they run tests. If they still repro we'll escalate with full logs.

Priya (Oncall): Marking P2 until customer confirms repro results. Thanks team.
